public_rationale: The operational deadline is June 2044. The search found substantial claimed AI-assisted physics progress, including OpenAI's October 2026 announcement. That announcement concerns particular mathematical results and their scientific examination, not accepted discovery of all physics. No examined event meets the early-resolution rule. Present non-occurrence cannot support a forecast whose deadline remains ahead.
limitations: A future outcome cannot directly prove that a probability judgment made in 2024 was well calibrated.
All of physics lacks a universally accepted completion criterion.
The latest company-reported result is not treated as independently validated by the announcement alone.
The accuracy of the attributed Altman quotation is not resolved here.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI discovering all of physics is neither coherent nor plausible within the next couple of decades.
public_payload.original_horizon_text: anytime in the next couple decades

statement.excerpt: Altman, for example, promised a week ago at Aspen Ideas that AI would “discover all of physics”, a claim that is neither coherent nor plausible anytime in the next couple decades.
statement.document_title: The need for a President that speaks AI natively

from_speaker: anytime in the next couple decades
our_interpretation: The ordinary forecast reading is that AI is not expected to discover essentially all of physics within approximately twenty years of the post.
Twenty years from June 28, 2024 gives June 28, 2044 as the operational deadline. The original wording is approximate.

All of physics requires broadly accepted, empirically grounded resolution of the field's fundamental outstanding questions, not isolated discoveries, benchmark performance, or mathematical treatment of existing theories.
The assessment concerns the forecasted scientific outcome. It does not treat the separate judgment about coherence as an objectively measurable event or invent a numerical probability threshold.
Whether Marcus quoted Altman accurately is separate from whether Marcus's forecast comes true.
criteria.support_condition: At the operational deadline, a broad scientific record establishes that fundamental physics remains substantially unresolved and AI has not achieved the stated comprehensive discovery.
criteria.contradiction_condition: By the deadline, independently validated AI contributions have achieved what the physics community broadly recognizes as essentially comprehensive discovery of fundamental physics.

evidence.locator: Existence of quantum chromodynamics and completions of the Standard Model section, final paragraphs
evidence.explanation: OpenAI reports a substantial mathematical result relevant to physics and an external collaboration to examine the work. This challenges any suggestion that AI cannot contribute to physics, but does not establish discovery of all physics or meet the early-resolution rule.
The authors describe both advances and unresolved verification challenges in AI-assisted physics. Their discussion does not establish either comprehensive discovery or its impossibility by 2044.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independently validated comprehensive scientific achievement could contradict the forecast early. Otherwise, assess the state of fundamental physics at the approximately 2044 deadline, retaining the stated ambiguity about completeness.
